// what this is: The anomaly guard's configuration for the local cluster lab, and the worked example a client copies.
Every metric name below was read out of the lab's own Prometheus rather than guessed — a name that
does not exist produces an empty result that Prometheus reports as success, which is the one failure
mode this whole subsystem exists to avoid.
A feature with no entry here is NOT a gap to paper over: its query is never issued and every cycle
counts it blind, which the guard prints at startup. CpuThrottleRatio and ErrorRate are left out on
purpose so that list has something in it on the first run.

_comment: NOT container_oom_events_total. Measured 2026-08-08 against a pod Kubernetes reported as OOMKilled
with exit 137: that series read 0 for the killed pod, and across 43 series cluster-wide over an hour
the only distinct value present was 0.0 - cAdvisor does not populate it on this runtime. The channel
bound, reported a number, satisfied every coverage check and could never fire.
kube-state-metrics carries the fact in two series: the restart increase says an event happened inside
the window, the last-terminated reason says it was an OOM. A name and a kind cannot express a join,
which is why 'query' exists. Verbatim queries carry their own range - keep [2m] in step with
OomEventsRate.query: sum by (pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{%selector%}[2m]) * on (namespace, pod, container) group_left() kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{%selector%,reason="OOMKilled"})
